current_flow: statement-model lays the story's foundation in four inseparable pieces. The budget parser now WALKS the workbook outline and records it as a per-batch snapshot carrying structure but no money, with each leaf given a stable key derived from its identity and written onto mis_budget itself so amounts and structure join without touching GL. The snapshot is persisted through IngestService and replaceBudgetBatch inside the same transaction that activates the batch. The Mapping Master gains a TAGGED target per entry - a workbook leaf or decision 0018's reserved unmapped-GL bucket - with a loader rejection for a triple claimed twice and an ingest-time drift check so a renamed line is reported rather than silently split. Finally the statement's own governed projection full-outer-joins Budget and Actual at leaf/month grain, filtering actuals by the resolved triples first per decision 0017 and receiving the triple-to-leaf mapping through a typed GovernedSelectionScope field, while the shipped (gl_code, month) relation and its six gated proofs stay untouched.
new_abstractions: a per-batch outline snapshot carrying structure but never money
a stable leaf key written onto mis_budget so amounts and structure join without GL
a tagged master target: a workbook leaf or the reserved unmapped-GL bucket
leafTargets on GovernedSelectionScope as the governed boundary for the mapping
an ingest-time mapping-drift check that reports rather than absorbs
gaps: P0 - c1 could not persist the snapshot at all: parseMisBudgetWorkbook returns period rows, IngestService.ingestBudget calls replaceBudgetBatch(metadata, rows), and the repository accepts only rows. Neither the ingest service nor its atomic-rollback test was in scope, so the outline had no route from parse to an activated batch.

P0 - the migration and the tests that pin it were out of scope: warehouse migrations are committed SQL under backend/drizzle-warehouse applied by the runner with journal metadata, and warehouse-schema.test.ts:223 pins the last migration as 0002. The 13-file budget was already fully allocated.

P0 - the budget-to-snapshot join was undefined. The plan said 'lineId to node', but the snapshot had no source-line field and mis_budget had no leaf_key. Joining on GL would re-merge exactly the 50001605 / 50001606 / 50001901 lines this story exists to split. Same-batch parent integrity was also undefined.

P0 - the unmapped-GL bucket had no valid leaf representation. Nine master entries deliberately resolve to the reserved bucket, not a workbook leaf, yet the plan simultaneously required every entry to carry a budget_leaf_key, every triple to resolve to a leaf, and leaf-less triples to become the bucket.

P1 - the proposed VALUES mapping could not reach SqlBuilder: GovernedSelectionScope carries triples and GL arrays only, and SelectionResolverService emits the same. Importing the global master inside the builder would bypass the injectable-master seam selection-resolution was fixed to establish.

P1 - structural reissue safety was asserted but not designed: renaming or renumbering a line changes its leaf key, which would silently split one statement line into a budget-only row and an actual-only row, with nothing checking the candidate snapshot against the master.

P1 - the mandatory DB proof was not required by the contract: verify_commands and required_tests were hermetic only, while the exact-totals and no-fan-out proof needs test:warehouse-proof with WAREHOUSE_DB_TEST=1, its quality-gate registration, an explicit host invocation and a dead-port negative control.

P1 - parent-footing ownership conflicted: task 1 produces only leaf/month rows, but its proof was written to assert every parent subtotal and the grand total, while the decomposition gives tree derivation to task 2.

P1 - the APPROVED story plan still contradicted decision 0022: its Scope section said to group the existing roll-up by the governed line so one query serves the statement, while its Technical Approach correctly required a separate projection. The stale line invited the prohibited composedCtes change.
P2 - reviewer_focus restated decisions but cited none of the governing constitution standards for module layout, interface naming, or the database and migration rules the task must follow.

The drift check's POLICY was undefined: the plan said drift is 'reported, never absorbed' but never said whether a workbook whose outline no longer matches the master's targets still loads. Failing closed blocks the client's upload; failing open risks a split statement line.
resolutions: The parse result now carries the outline, replaceBudgetBatch takes and persists it INSIDE the same transaction that writes the rows and activates the batch, and ingest.service.ts plus ingest.service.test.ts are in write_scope. A snapshot that survived a rolled-back batch would be worse than none.

backend/drizzle-warehouse/, warehouse-migrate.ts and warehouse-schema.test.ts are in write_scope, and the plan states that the new table, column and view, the journal metadata and the pinned last-migration number move together. The budget is raised to 20 files / 2600 lines with a stated reason.

mis_budget itself gains a leaf_key column written by the parser, so the amount row and its snapshot node share one key and there is NO join on GL. Uniqueness is enforced per (batch_id, period, leaf_key) and parent_key must reference a node in the SAME batch.

A master entry's target is now TAGGED - either {kind: leaf, leafKey} or {kind: bucket} for decision 0018's reserved unmapped-GL line. The nine bucket triples are not forced to invent a leaf. A bucket row carries zero Budget and its own Actual, sits as a distinct top-level line, and still counts toward the grand total so the slice reconciles to the full DUB total.

GovernedSelectionScope and SelectionResolverService gain a typed leafTargets entry mapping (plant, costCentre, glCode) to its tagged target, so the mapping reaches the builder through the governed boundary. selection-resolver.service.ts, its interface and its test are in write_scope, and importing MAPPING_MASTER inside the builder is explicitly forbidden in reviewer_focus.

Budget ingest now validates the candidate snapshot's leaf keys against the master's declared targets and records any target with no matching leaf in the batch validation result, the way the uncomputed roll-over count already is. A FOURTH required test proves drift is reported rather than silently splitting the line.

The gated statement-projection.db.test.ts is registered in test:warehouse-proof and in the quality-gate expected-script registry, both of which are in write_scope, and the Manual Verification step makes the host invocation and the dead-port negative control explicit - the D-0008 pattern this project already uses.

Ownership is split at the grain each task actually produces: task 1 proves leaf-grain exactness, the three-way split and no fan-out; parent-by-parent footing moves to task 2, which owns tree derivation. Stated in both the acceptance criterion and the Manual Verification step.

The contradictory Scope bullet is REMOVED from the active plan and the draft: it now says the statement adds its own governed projection at leaf/month grain and leaves the (gl_code, month) relation untouched, matching decision 0022 and the plan's own Technical Approach. The story plan must therefore be re-approved on the board before this task starts.

reviewer_focus now cites constitution/03-modular-monolith-structure.md and pnp-coding-standards-modular-monolith.md for module layout and the .interface.ts naming rule, the database and migration standards for the new table, column and view, and decision 0015 for warehouse snake_case.

HUMAN-decided (round): the ingest SUCCEEDS and the unmatched master targets are recorded in the batch validation result, the way the uncomputed roll-over count already is - Srihari is never blocked from loading a new plan, and the drift is visible for us to reconcile the master. Flagging drifted lines on the statement itself was rejected as reaching into tasks 2 and 3, beyond this task's scope.
open_items: The story plan changed to remove its decision-0022 contradiction, so it must be re-approved on the board before this task starts.
Parent-by-parent footing is task 2's proof, not this task's.
The budget-leaf correspondence stays provisional until Srihari confirms it.

rounds.question: Task 1 adds a drift check: when a budget workbook is re-uploaded, the parser compares its outline's leaf keys against the ones the Mapping Master targets. If Srihari renames or renumbers a line, its key changes and a master entry now points at nothing — which, unchecked, silently splits one statement line into a budget-only row and an actual-only row. The check itself is settled; what it should DO is not. What should happen to that upload?
options: Refuse the upload until the master is reconciled
Load it, and mark the affected lines on the statement

summary: One cold read returned ten findings, four of them P0, and every one was repository-answerable - no human round was needed. The four blockers were all the same kind of gap: a contract that could not reach the code it needed. The outline had no route from parse to an activated batch (the ingest service and repository were out of scope); the migration and the test pinning its number were out of scope; the budget-to-snapshot join was undefined and would have fallen back to GL, re-merging the very lines the story exists to split; and the unmapped-GL bucket had no valid leaf representation for its nine triples. The contract now carries a leaf_key on mis_budget, a tagged leaf-or-bucket master target, a typed leafTargets field so the mapping reaches the builder through the governed boundary rather than a global import, an ingest-time drift check with its own required test, the D-0008 registration and negative control, and a 20-file / 2600-line budget with a stated reason. Parent footing moved to task 2, which owns tree derivation. The grill also caught a stale line in the APPROVED story plan that still contradicted decision 0022 and invited the prohibited composedCtes change; it is removed, which means the plan needs re-approval on the board. Verdict pass.

criteria_map.The budget parser walks the workbook out: KEEP (amended). The outline snapshot survives, but the grill showed it had no route to storage and no defined join. The criterion now requires parent_key to reference a node in the SAME batch, mis_budget to carry the same leaf_key so amounts and structure join without touching GL, and the snapshot to be written INSIDE the transaction that activates the batch.
criteria_map.The Mapping Master records a TAGGED targ: KEEP (amended). The correspondence survives, but a bare budget_leaf_key could not represent the nine triples that deliberately resolve to decision 0018's reserved bucket. The target is now TAGGED - leaf or bucket - the loader rejects one triple claimed for two targets, and ingest validates candidate leaf keys against the master so a renamed line is reported as drift rather than silently splitting a statement line.
criteria_map.The statement's governed projection retu: KEEP (amended). The projection survives, but the mapping had no way to reach the builder: GovernedSelectionScope carries triples and GL arrays only. It now travels as a typed leafTargets field through the governed boundary rather than a global master import. Parent-by-parent footing moved OUT to task 2, which owns tree derivation; this task proves the leaf grain it actually produces.
